title: Reduce prompt-ingest overhead via kernel hinting, session-level lexeme shards, and ASCII fast path
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: The runtime currently spends disproportionate CPU and scheduling overhead on prompt preprocessing (canonicalization, lexemeization, and UTF-8 normalization) for short, high-throughput requests. This task proposes a combined approach: (1) expose lightweight kernel-hinting metadata so the serving runtime can prefer ascii/vectorized normalization kernels when input distribution qualifies; (2) implement a session-level sharded lexeme cache that lives on the prefill side to amortize repeated prefixes and prompt templates; (3) add an ASCII fast-path that short-circuits the full normalization pipeline for common English prompts. Goal: reduce per-request preprocess CPU and tail latency without sacrificing correctness for non-ASCII inputs.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end median ingest latency improvement >= 20% on synthetic short-prompt workload
Per-request CPU cycles for preprocessing reduced >= 30% for ascii-dominant inputs
No correctness regressions: normalized token sequences must match baseline for a validated prompt set
Session-level lexeme cache hit-rate >= 40% on our internal usage trace during canary
Feature toggles exist to opt-out fast-paths and kernel-hinting per-customer
technical_notes: Kernel hinting: extend model config with `ingest_kernel_hint` (values: auto|ascii_fast|utf8_vectorized). Router attaches hint to inbound request metadata.

Session-level lexeme shards: small, fixed-size LRU per worker-thread using 64B fingerprint keys to avoid full-string storage; shards keyed by (customer_id, session_id, template_hash) to limit cross-customer leakage.
ASCII fast-path: vectorized path that skips Unicode normalization if bytes are in 0x00-0x7F and whitespace/tokenization heuristics are satisfied.
Graceful fallback: if fast-path fails (non-ascii detected, or normalization mismatch) fall back to standard pipeline and populate shard to avoid repeated misses.
Metrics: add `ingest.preprocess.cpu_ns`, `ingest.preprocess.latency_ms`, `ingest.cache.hit_rate`, and labels for `kernel_hint` and `fastpath` to attribute savings.
Safety: ensure per-customer memory caps for shards and strict eviction semantics; never persist raw prompt bytes outside worker memory.
Compatibility: existing SDKs unaffected; kernel-hint defaults to auto so behavior is opt-in via model config or runtime policy.
implementation_plan: 1) Design API: add `ingest_kernel_hint` to model manifest and update runtime config parsing (owner: Marco)
2) Implement session shard LRU cache in C++ serving runtime with tight allocation bounds (owner: Priya)
3) Implement ascii fast-path normalization in the hot ingest lane and unit tests (owner: Rafael)
4) Wire router to attach kernel_hint metadata for known/curated models (owner: SRE)
5) Add feature flags behind runtime toggle and console UI toggle for canary customers (owner: Console team)
6) Add telemetry and dashboards for hit-rate and per-kernel latency (owner: Observability)
7) Run canary against 3 internal customers, collect metrics, run canary load tests, iterate (owner: Marco)
8) Ramp to 25% production traffic with monitoring alerts, then full release when SLOs stable (owner: Release eng)
Estimated effort breakdown: kernel-hint API (1), session cache (2), ascii fast-path (3), e2e tests and canary (2)
testing_plan: Unit tests for ascii fast-path correctness against our normalization corpus
Fuzzing to ensure fallback paths triggered appropriately for edge unicode sequences
Microbenchmarks: compare cycles/token for ascii vs baseline across microbatch sizes
Load tests: 2k RPS short-prompt workload with mixed customers to measure hit-rate and tail latencies
Regression suite to ensure no change in tokenization result for the representative eval set
rollout_notes: Start with an internal-only canary: config on a subset of workers with kernel_hint forced to ascii_fast for synthetic workloads
Enable session shards only on workers with >16GB free RAM; limit per-shard memory to 128KB by default
Expose console metric for shard eviction pressure; auto-disable fast-path if eviction rate > 5%
Provide a runtime toggle (`ingest_fastpath.enabled`) and model-level override to opt specific customers out
Post-launch: 2-week observation window, then evaluate for inclusion in runtime-1.21 default config
